topic: Claude Mythos vs GPT-5.4 vs Gemini 3.1 Pro: 2026 Frontier Model Comparison

key_points: Frames Mythos as the coding leader, GPT-5.4 as strongest for professional knowledge work and computer use, and Gemini 3.1 Pro as the price-performance winner.
Uses benchmark-heavy comparison tables for SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench, GPQA Diamond, ARC-AGI-2, Humanity's Last Exam, GDPval, pricing, and context windows.
Reader intent is practical model selection by use case: coding, desktop automation, scientific reasoning, long-context analysis, professional knowledge work, and agentic workflows.
Focuses on April 2026 benchmark deltas among Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4, and Gemini 3.1 Pro, especially GPQA Diamond.
Treats small reasoning-score gaps as meaningful because mature reasoning benchmarks are difficult to move.
Does not fully center Claude Mythos, so a Mythos-led article can differentiate by adding access, safety, and release-status context.
Compares GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.6, and Gemini 3.1 Pro through production concerns: provider availability, context limits, output limits, pricing, and routing strategy.
Recommends evaluating GPT-5.4 in a local benchmark suite rather than assuming it wins from launch claims.
Highlights model routing and API gateway switching as a practical way to reduce lock-in.
Targets the exact comparison query and emphasizes Claude Mythos's unusual position: powerful but constrained by access and safety considerations.
Includes sections on side-by-side numbers, coding performance, reasoning and science, cybersecurity, pricing, access, and when to use each model.
The unique ranking opportunity is to be more current on the June 2026 Mythos/Fable restrictions and public-access uncertainty.
Community discussion compiles benchmark rows for Claude Mythos, Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4, and Gemini 3.1 Pro from Anthropic system-card tables.
Useful for identifying reader skepticism: users question whether headline benchmark gains are large enough and whether benchmark contamination is a concern.
A strong article should explicitly separate lab claims, independent benchmarks, and practical eval advice.

stats.fact: Anthropic says Claude Mythos 5 is the latest update for Mythos Preview, with gains in cybersecurity, biology, and healthcare benchmarks, but access is limited to a small group of vetted partners.
Anthropic said Project Glasswing was expanded to approximately 150 new organizations in more than fifteen countries on June 2, 2026.
OpenAI says GPT-5.4 is available in ChatGPT as GPT-5.4 Thinking, in the API, and in Codex, with GPT-5.4 Pro also available for maximum performance on complex tasks.
OpenAI reports GPT-5.4 supports up to a 1M-token context window in Codex and the API and has native computer-use capabilities for agent workflows across applications.
OpenAI reports GPT-5.4 reached 83.0% wins or ties on GDPval, 57.7% on SWE-Bench Pro Public, 75.0% on OSWorld-Verified, 54.6% on Toolathlon, and 82.7% on BrowseComp.
OpenAI reports GPT-5.4 responses were 33% less likely to contain false individual claims and 18% less likely to contain any factual errors than GPT-5.2 on a de-identified user-flagged prompt set.
OpenAI listed GPT-5.4 API pricing at $2.50 per million input tokens, $0.25 per million cached input tokens, and $15 per million output tokens.
Google says Gemini 3.1 Pro is its most advanced reasoning Gemini model and can handle text, audio, images, video, PDFs, and entire code repositories with a 1M-token context window.
Google says Gemini 3.1 Pro is rolling out to developers, enterprises, and consumers and is designed for advanced reasoning tasks such as synthesizing data and explaining complex topics.
Business Insider reported on June 15, 2026 that U.S. export controls forced Anthropic to disable Fable 5 and Mythos 5 broadly after officials raised security concerns.

Axios reported on June 15, 2026 that cybersecurity leaders argued restrictions on Anthropic's Mythos-class models could hurt defenders more than attackers, because similar proof-of-concept vulnerability capabilities exist across other frontier models.

angles: The honest answer is not one winner: Mythos is the high-risk, high-capability specialist; GPT-5.4 is the professional-agent workhorse; Gemini 3.1 Pro is the long-context and multimodal value pick.

Availability is now a first-class comparison axis. A model that wins benchmarks but is restricted to vetted partners or affected by export controls may be less usable than a slightly weaker public API.

Do not rank models from a single benchmark table. Separate coding, tool use, computer use, long-context retrieval, multimodal understanding, scientific reasoning, safety policy, and cost per completed task.
Security policy is part of product quality in 2026. Mythos/Fable restrictions turned capability governance into a buying criterion for enterprises and security teams.
Benchmark contamination and vendor-selected evals are a reader concern. Recommend teams run task-specific evals against their own repos, documents, workflows, latency budgets, and safety policies.
Cost should be discussed per completed workflow, not just per million tokens, because reasoning effort, retries, context size, cache hit rate, and tool-call failures can reverse headline pricing.
